question: The rock-cut Kailasa temple at Ellora was carved out of how many rocks?
solution:
The correct answer is __**One single rock**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The **Kailasa Temple** at Ellora, located in the **Aurangabad district of Maharashtra, India**, is a remarkable example of ancient Indian rock-cut architecture. 
• This temple is unique as it was **carved out of a single monolithic rock**, making it one of the largest monolithic structures in the world. 
• It was constructed during the reign of the **Rashtrakuta dynasty** under the rule of **King Krishna I** in the 8th century CE. 
• The temple is dedicated to **Lord Shiva** and is designed to resemble Mount Kailash, the mythical abode of Lord Shiva in Hindu mythology. 
• The excavation and carving process involved the removal of approximately **200,000 tons of rock**, showcasing the advanced engineering and artistic skills of the time. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Architectural Features:** 
• The Kailasa Temple features intricate carvings, including **sculptures of deities, mythical creatures, and scenes from Hindu epics like the Ramayana and Mahabharata**. 
• The temple has a **multi-tiered structure** with a central shrine, a Nandi pavilion, and a series of mandapas (halls). 
• The intricate details of the carvings reflect the **Dravidian style of architecture**. 
• **Historical Significance:** 
• The Kailasa Temple represents the **culmination of centuries of rock-cut architecture** in India. 
• It is believed to have taken **nearly 20 years** to complete, involving thousands of laborers and artisans. 
• The temple stands as a testament to the **technological and artistic prowess** of ancient India. 
• **Other Notable Rock-Cut Structures at Ellora:** 
• Ellora is home to **34 rock-cut caves**, which include Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain temples and monasteries. 
• The site is a UNESCO **World Heritage Site** and attracts tourists and scholars from around the globe. 
• **Comparison with Other Rock-Cut Temples:** 
• The Kailasa Temple is often compared to the rock-cut temples of Mahabalipuram and Ajanta, showcasing the evolution of rock-cut techniques. 
• Unlike the Ajanta caves, which are primarily Buddhist, the Kailasa Temple is distinctly **Hindu in theme and symbolism**. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• The construction of the Kailasa Temple involved a unique top-down excavation method, starting from the top of the rock and working downward, which prevented structural collapse. 
• The temple aligns with the principles of **Vastu Shastra**, an ancient Indian architectural science. 
• The site of Ellora demonstrates the **religious harmony** of ancient India, as it includes structures representing Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism. 
• The Kailasa Temple is often regarded as one of the **seven wonders of India** due to its architectural brilliance and historical significance. </ul
